ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, point $E$ is a point outside the square $ABCD$, and $ED=CD$, connect $AE$ and intersect $BD$ at point $F$. If $\angle CDE=30^\circ$, then what is the measure of $\angle DFC$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution}: 
Since quadrilateral $ABCD$ is a square,\\ 
thus $AD=DC, \angle ADC=90^\circ$,\\ 
therefore $\angle ADB=\angle BDC=45^\circ$,\\ 
since $DC=DE$,\\ 
thus $AD=DE$,\\ 
therefore $\angle DAE=\angle DEA$,\\ 
since $\angle ADE=90^\circ+30^\circ=120^\circ$,\\ 
thus $\angle DAE=\frac{180^\circ−120^\circ}{2}=30^\circ$,\\ 
therefore $\angle AFD=180^\circ−30^\circ−45^\circ=105^\circ$,\\ 
In $\triangle ADF$ and $\triangle CDF$,\\ 
since $\left\{\begin{array}{c}AD=DC\\ \angle ADB=\angle BDC\\ DF=DF\end{array}\right.$,\\ 
thus $\triangle ADF\cong \triangle CDF$,\\ 
therefore $\angle DFC=\angle AFD=\boxed{105^\circ}$.

raw_record.original_question: As shown in the figure, point $E$ is outside square $ABCD$, and $ED=CD$. Connect $AE$ and let it intersect $BD$ at point $F$. If $\angle CDE=30^\circ$, what is the measure of $\angle DFC$?
raw_record.answer: Solution: Since quadrilateral $ABCD$ is a square, $AD=DC$ and $\angle ADC=90^\circ$. Therefore $\angle ADB=\angle BDC=45^\circ$. Since $DC=DE$, we have $AD=DE$, so $\angle DAE=\angle DEA$. Also, $\angle ADE=90^\circ+30^\circ=120^\circ$, thus $\angle DAE=\frac{180^\circ-120^\circ}{2}=30^\circ$. Therefore $\angle AFD=180^\circ-30^\circ-45^\circ=105^\circ$. In $\triangle ADF$ and $\triangle CDF$, since $AD=DC$, $\angle ADB=\angle BDC$, and $DF=DF$, the two triangles are congruent. Therefore $\angle DFC=\angle AFD=105^\circ$.
raw_record.final_cot:
First describe the image: In the figure is square ABCD, A is at the upper left, B is at the lower left, C is at the lower right, D is at the upper right; point E is outside on the right side of the square. Segment AE intersects the square's diagonal BD at F, and CF, CD, DE are also drawn in the figure, and the conditions ED=CD and ∠CDE=30° are given.

Then reason: Because ABCD is a square, AD=CD, and ∠ADC=90°. Also because ED=CD, AD=ED, triangle ADE is an isosceles triangle. From the figure, E is in the outside direction of CD, ∠ADE=∠ADC+∠CDE=90°+30°=120°. Therefore the two base angles of triangle ADE are equal, ∠DAE=∠AED=(180°-120°)/2=30°.

BD is the diagonal of the square, so it bisects ∠ADC, obtaining ∠ADB=45°. Since F is on AE and F is on BD, in triangle ADF, ∠DAF=30°, ∠ADF=45°, so ∠AFD=180°-30°-45°=105°.

Finally, the square is symmetric about diagonal BD, the symmetric point of A about BD is C, while D and F remain fixed on BD, so ray FA is symmetric to FC, hence ∠DFC=∠AFD=105°.
